master.Safety / Compatibility Notes: Keep off skin and away from heat; dispose of oiled rags in a closed metal can, never balled in an open bin
master.SOP Integration Notes: Garage Zones 1, 2 and 6 Shine input; the oiled wipe that stops rust at the handle end

master.Primary Purpose: Lift oil and fluid staining out of a garage or workshop slab
master.Preferred Organizer / Installation: Cleaning caddy
master.Safety / Compatibility Notes: Ventilate while working; keep off skin and eyes; never flush residue to a storm drain
master.SOP Integration Notes: Garage slab pass; the once-properly degrease that makes a pale floor readable

master.Primary Purpose: Draw fresh oil and fluid spots up out of concrete before sweeping off
master.Preferred Organizer / Installation: Beside the parking bay
master.Safety / Compatibility Notes: Sweep up and dispose of used granules as contaminated waste, never to a drain
master.SOP Integration Notes: Garage Zone 4 Shine input; leave on the old stains overnight before the degrease

master.Primary Purpose: Clean battery contacts and charger terminals without leaving residue
master.Preferred Organizer / Installation: Cleaning caddy
master.Safety / Compatibility Notes: Power down and unplug first; use in ventilation; never a damp cloth on contacts
master.SOP Integration Notes: Garage Zone 3 Shine input; corrosion on pack rails and charger terminals

master.Primary Purpose: Scrape caked soil and rust off blades and concrete before cleaning
master.Preferred Organizer / Installation: Cleaning caddy
master.Safety / Compatibility Notes: Wear eye protection; flying rust and grit is the reason this is a safety-glasses job
master.SOP Integration Notes: Garage Zone 6 Shine input; scrape, oil, then file the cutting edge

master.Primary Purpose: Sweep a slab or hard floor in a single pass to hold a degreased surface
master.Preferred Organizer / Installation: Wall rail or tool clips
master.Safety / Compatibility Notes: Hang head-up on a rail; bristles resting on concrete splay and re-soil the floor they touch
master.SOP Integration Notes: Garage slab Sustain input; after one proper degrease, a sweep is what holds it

master.Primary Purpose: Reach overhead racks, roof decks, and high shelving from the floor
master.Preferred Organizer / Installation: Wall hook
master.Safety / Compatibility Notes: Use from the floor rather than climbing where you can; wear eye protection under overhead dust
master.SOP Integration Notes: Garage Zone 7 Shine input; the lid dust that tells you how long a bin has sat

master.Primary Purpose: Reach overhead storage safely with both hands free to carry down
master.Preferred Organizer / Installation: Hung flat on a wall rail
master.Safety / Compatibility Notes: Open fully and set level; never work from a ladder rocking on a sloped slab, and never carry a bin down without a hand for the stile
master.SOP Integration Notes: Garage Zone 7; nothing goes overhead that you cannot lift down with both hands on a stable ladder

master.Primary Purpose: Lift dried glue and finish off a bench top without marking the surface
master.Preferred Organizer / Installation: Cleaning caddy
master.Safety / Compatibility Notes: Plastic rather than steel so the bench top is not gouged; work flat to the surface
master.SOP Integration Notes: Workshop Zone 1 Shine input; scrape squeeze-out before it telegraphs into the next workpiece

master.Primary Purpose: Take baked pitch and resin off saw blades and cutters so they cut clean
master.Preferred Organizer / Installation: Cleaning caddy
master.Safety / Compatibility Notes: Unplug the tool and remove the blade first; wear gloves and eye protection; ventilate
master.SOP Integration Notes: Workshop Zone 2 Shine input; a pitched blade burns the cut rather than making it

master.Primary Purpose: Clean brushes and finishing tools through to the ferrule
master.Preferred Organizer / Installation: Flammable safety cabinet
master.Safety / Compatibility Notes: Flammable: store in the metal cabinet away from any pilot or heater, ventilate while using, and dispose of via household hazardous waste, never a drain
master.SOP Integration Notes: Workshop Zone 5 Shine input; match the cleaner to the finish family

master.Primary Purpose: Contain oil, stain, and solvent rags in a lidded metal can that shuts on its own weight
master.Preferred Organizer / Installation: Beside the finishing zone
master.Safety / Compatibility Notes: Oil-finish rags generate their own heat as they cure and can ignite with nothing touching them; the lid must fall shut on its own weight
master.SOP Integration Notes: Workshop Zone 5 and Garage Zone 1; the single highest-value safety purchase in either room

master.Primary Purpose: Put out a small fire at the point it starts, mounted where it can be reached
master.Preferred Organizer / Installation: Wall bracket by the door
master.Safety / Compatibility Notes: Mount on a bracket with clear floor in front of it; check the gauge sits in the green and write the inspection date on the bracket
master.SOP Integration Notes: Workshop Zone 6; taught in Chapter 22, prevent and prepare

master.Primary Purpose: Treat the cuts, splinters, and burns a working room actually produces
master.Preferred Organizer / Installation: Wall-mounted beside the PPE board
master.Safety / Compatibility Notes: Keep burn dressings in it, not just plasters; date the lid and re-check when the extinguisher is checked
master.SOP Integration Notes: Workshop Zone 6; a kit quietly raided for household plasters is not a first aid kit

master.Product Standard Name: Scraper and absorbent entry mat set
master.Primary Purpose: Stop grit and water at the threshold in two stages, one mat outside to scrape and one inside to soak
master.Preferred Organizer / Installation: Laid outside and inside the door, squared to the frame
master.Safety / Compatibility Notes: Lay flat with no curled edge, which is a trip hazard at a doorway; shake the outside mat and dry the inside one on the same day
master.SOP Integration Notes: Mudroom threshold layer one and two; the boot tray is layer three. Grit ground underfoot sands the finish off a floor

master.Primary Purpose: Scrub caked mud and salt out of a boot tray, a bin, or an outdoor surface
master.Preferred Organizer / Installation: Hung by the outside tap or in the caddy
master.Safety / Compatibility Notes: Work outdoors where the run-off goes to ground rather than into a household drain
master.SOP Integration Notes: Mudroom Zone 3 Shine input; a dried-out boot tray turns to dust and gets walked back inside

master.Primary Purpose: Lift hair and street dust off coat shoulders and bag straps without marking the fabric
master.Preferred Organizer / Installation: Hung at the end of the coat run
master.Safety / Compatibility Notes: Brush with the weave, not against it; keep it away from wet fabric so it does not felt the nap
master.SOP Integration Notes: Mudroom Zone 1 Shine input; the tops of hanging coats are where the room settles its dust

master.Product Standard Name: Grill grate scraper or coiled brush
master.Primary Purpose: Scrape carbonised residue off cooking grates without shedding bristles
master.Preferred Organizer / Installation: Hung on the grill tool rack
master.Safety / Compatibility Notes: Bristle-free by design. A wire brush that sheds a bristle onto a grate can put it into food, which is why this type replaces one rather than supplementing it. Retire any brush whose bristles pull free by hand.
master.SOP Integration Notes: Used at the end of every cook while the grates are still hot, and again with the degreaser when the grates come out.

master.Primary Purpose: Scrub decking boards and stair treads from standing height
master.Preferred Organizer / Installation: Hung head up on the tool wall clips
master.Safety / Compatibility Notes: Stiff enough for algae film, soft enough not to raise the grain on softwood. Work with the grain of the boards.
master.SOP Integration Notes: The primary tool of the Surface, Rail, and Safety Zone. Scrubbing the shaded treads is the single highest-value cleaning act on the property after rain.

master.Primary Purpose: Clean outdoor cushion and canopy fabric without stripping its water resistance
master.Preferred Organizer / Installation: Stored in the cleaning caddy, indoors over winter
master.Safety / Compatibility Notes: Never mix with any other cleaner. Test on a hidden seam first. Cushions must dry all the way through before they go back under a lid.
master.SOP Integration Notes: Used with a soft brush and a blotting action rather than a soak. Sponge, stand the cushion on its edge, and let both faces dry in air.

master.Primary Purpose: Float loose grit off outdoor furniture, decking, and pots before any cleaner is applied
master.Preferred Organizer / Installation: Wound on the hose reel, drained before frost
master.Safety / Compatibility Notes: Drain and disconnect before the first frost. Never run a hose across the walking route between the door and the steps.
master.SOP Integration Notes: Rinsing comes FIRST outdoors, which inverts the indoor dry-before-wet rule. Floating the grit off before scrubbing is what stops the grit acting as an abrasive.
